checks.summary: 73 passed across 7 directly related suites. Five actual production-hook browser REDs became green: restored document.hasFocus without window focus event, with/without visibility return event, background-born public seat, DOM hiding during active paint, and actual focus loss without blur. Actual session-view unmount, background received text, remount baseline and later append also pass. Real production compact flow, execution feed, assistant seat, ReasoningRow/DisclosureRow and Markdown renderer remain in the fixture; previous final-boundary, two-owner/two-turn batches, epoch, handoff, reading and history cases continue passing. Synthetic focus tests now set document.hasFocus alongside events, so missing-event return is independently testable. output/assistant-reveal-focus-return-1023/focused.json and red-summary.json.

Actual full frontend patch entry completes twice via in-memory write overlay. 30 virtual assets; protected reply/listener regions stable, guards preserved, module syntax valid and zero dependency writes. Complete asset byte equality remains false due to unrelated existing sink ordering.
Passed on exact committed source.
Passed; focused two-file successor.

uiVerification.summary: Isolated Chromium exercises real production execution routing, actual ReasoningRow/DisclosureRow and complete semantic Markdown. The document focus API changes independently of window focus events. Background batches remain fully readable; the first restored current content is baselined once; genuinely later public text regains neighboring character alpha and a pending suffix. Session view closes while text continues in its stored state, returns without replay, then later actual append fades. No GUI, actual model call, installed dependency write or shared build was performed. Integrated native app-switch verification remains root-owned.

acceptanceCriteria: When document.hasFocus exists it is read live instead of trusting the cached window-focus event state; the event cache remains a fallback only for environments lacking the API.
Visibility availability is captured before skipNext; every unavailable update retains the return-baseline flag rather than consuming it in the background.
Active paint which discovers actual focus loss, DOM hiding or disconnection suspends the current visual queue and marks the next current content as a baseline, even without blur/workspace events.
Returning without a window focus event exposes prior background content immediately once; genuinely later appended public text resumes gradual character reveal.

Existing epoch, fresh/live history gates, trusted same-commit final handoff, reading quiet period, reasoning exclusion and real native/Research following continue passing; background generation itself is not cancelled.
risks: The user confirmed switching apps or sessions during the failed response. The deterministic missing-window-focus and background-render-pause paths now reproduce and are fixed. Native OS app-switch verification on the integrated package remains root-owned.

On foreground return the first current content deliberately becomes a complete baseline to avoid replaying background catch-up; later actual arrivals fade. Already received background content is not animated retroactively.
The full patch re-entry verifier reports complete asset byte inequality from unrelated existing sink insertion order; protected reply regions, guards and syntax are stable.
